newsitem.title: USA: Payment in question on Palm Beach Cty, Fla., bonds.
newsitem.headline: Payment in question on Palm Beach Cty, Fla., bonds.

text.p: It was still unclear Monday whether the owners of two cogeneration plants in Palm Beach County, Fla., would make the next debt service payment on the bonds that financed the plants.
"The determination on whether or not that will be paid has not been made," said Lisa Donnellan of U.S. Generating, a consultant for the plant owners.
However, the next payment on the bonds is due on July 1 and not June 1 as previously reported by Reuters and other news media, Donnellan said.
The plants are owned by the Okeelanta Power and Gator Generating Company Limited Partnerships, which filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy reorganization last month.
The partnerships are owned by Pacific Gas & Electric Co., a unit of PG&E Corp and Bechtel Enterprises.
The plants burn waste products from sugarcane processing. Palm Beach County issued three series of industrial development revenue bonds for the plants:
--$160 million of tax-exempt Okeelanta Power Limited Partnership Project, Series 1993A
--$120.5 million of Osceola Power Limited Partnership Project, tax-exempt Series 1994 A
--$8 million of Osceola Power Limited Partnership Project, taxable Series 1994B.
The next debt service payment is about $4.6 million on the Osceola bonds and $5.4 million on the Okeelanta bonds, Donnellan said.
The bonds are in technical default because of the bankruptcy filing but no payments have been missed.
